posture: Inform — a clean, quiet scan. The 6–7 August window produced nothing that both clears the REZ relevance bar and is genuinely new against the prior three digests (3, 5 and 6 August), so an empty digest is published to preserve archive continuity and confirm the scan ran clean. The dominant threads remain live but were already logged and are deduplicated out here: the NSW Legislative Council Portfolio Committee No. 4 final report (tabled 29 July, 25 findings/16 recommendations, 'predictable and avoidable' harm, a specific finding that EnergyCo failed its central coordinating role and that consultation gave communities no meaningful influence, and a three-month clock — to roughly end October — for a government implementation plan with six-monthly reporting to Parliament, plus recommendations for an independent landholder advocate, formalised EnergyCo accountability metrics and recurrent council funding); Upper Hunter Shire Council's 28 July resolution asking the state to pause New England land acquisition; EnergyCo's deferral of the New England (Muswellbrook–Armidale) aerial survey to September; and the close of the public submission window (6 August) on EnergyCo's draft New England REZ Access Scheme Declaration, which now passes to the Minister for Energy to weigh before any formal declaration. On delivery, the New England EIS remains expected to be lodged and go on public exhibition in the second half of 2026 (no lodgement yet), and Central-West Orana transmission construction continues (first tower raised April 2026) — both context, not new signal. Paid mastheads (AFR, SMH and the ACM regional titles) surfaced only recycled coverage of the inquiry, corridor, construction and grants stories at headline level and were not opened. Net: no new decision-grade or developing signal today.
